Research/2025-26/Computational astrophysics

Computational astrophysics

Primordial Black Holes and Population III Star Formation

An exploratory particle simulation of how central black-hole mass relates to star formation in an early-galaxy model.

Research question

What did the project ask?

In a particle-based early-galaxy model, how does the mass of a central primordial black hole affect the formation of Population III stars?

Significance

Why does it matter?

Early black holes and primordial stars may influence one another's formation, shaping models of the first galaxies and black-hole growth.

Method

What did the team do?

The team built a C++ smoothed-particle-hydrodynamics simulation with Barnes-Hut gravity, quadtree neighbor searches, leapfrog integration, an isothermal gas model, and a Jeans-density star-formation threshold, then compared runs with different central black-hole masses.

Principal result

What did the evidence show?

In this exploratory model, higher central black-hole masses were associated with fewer stars at the end of a run. The fitted final star count declined approximately exponentially with black-hole mass; the model did not include black-hole growth or radiative feedback.
